title: Levels of Organisation
content:
# Levels of Organisation

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe the hierarchy of organisation in multicellular organisms
- Define cell, tissue, organ, organ system, and organism
- Give examples of each level of organisation in animals and plants
- Explain how the levels of organisation are related

## Introduction

Multicellular organisms are highly organised. Cells don't just exist randomly - they are organised into increasingly complex structures that work together. This organisation follows a hierarchy, from the simplest level (cells) to the most complex (the whole organism).

## Key Concepts

### The Hierarchy of Organisation

```
Cells → Tissues → Organs → Organ Systems → Organism
```

[DIAGRAM: Pyramid showing levels of organisation from cells at the bottom to organism at the top]

Each level is made up of the previous level working together:
- Similar **cells** group together to form **tissues**
- Different **tissues** group together to form **organs**
- **Organs** work together in **organ systems**
- **Organ systems** work together to form an **organism**

### Level 1: Cells

**Definition:** The basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

- Smallest unit that can carry out life processes
- Specialised cells have specific functions
- Examples: nerve cells, muscle cells, red blood cells, palisade cells

### Level 2: Tissues

**Definition:** A group of similar cells working together to perform a specific function.

**Types of Animal Tissues:**

| Tissue Type | Description | Examples |
|-------------|-------------|----------|
| Epithelial tissue | Covers surfaces and lines cavities | Skin, lining of intestines, airways |
| Muscle tissue | Can contract to cause movement | Skeletal, cardiac, smooth muscle |
| Nervous tissue | Transmits electrical impulses | Brain, spinal cord, nerves |
| Connective tissue | Supports, connects, or separates other tissues | Bone, cartilage, blood, fat |

**Types of Plant Tissues:**

| Tissue Type | Description | Examples |
|-------------|-------------|----------|
| Epidermal tissue | Outer protective layer | Leaf epidermis, root epidermis |
| Palisade mesophyll | Main photosynthetic tissue | Upper layer of leaf |
| Spongy mesophyll | Gas exchange tissue | Lower layer of leaf |
| Xylem | Water transport tissue | Throughout stem, roots, leaves |
| Phloem | Sugar transport tissue | Throughout stem, roots, leaves |
| Meristematic tissue | Growth tissue | Root tips, shoot tips |

[DIAGRAM: Different types of animal and plant tissues]

### Level 3: Organs

**Definition:** A structure made of different tissues working together to perform a specific function.

**Examples of Animal Organs:**

| Organ | Main Tissues | Function |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| Heart | Cardiac muscle, connective, epithelial, nervous | Pumps blood |
| Stomach | Muscle, epithelial, connective, glandular | Digests food |
| Lungs | Epithelial, connective, muscle | Gas exchange |
| Brain | Nervous tissue, connective | Controls body functions |
| Skin | Epithelial, connective, muscle, nervous | Protection, temperature regulation |
| Liver | Epithelial, connective | Metabolism, detoxification |

**Examples of Plant Organs:**

| Organ | Main Tissues | Function |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| Leaf | Epidermis, palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll, xylem, phloem | Photosynthesis |
| Root | Epidermis, cortex, xylem, phloem | Absorption, anchorage |
| Stem | Epidermis, cortex, xylem, phloem | Support, transport |
| Flower | Various specialised tissues | Reproduction |

[DIAGRAM: Cross-section of a leaf showing different tissues forming the organ]

### Level 4: Organ Systems

**Definition:** A group of organs working together to perform a major function.

**Human Organ Systems:**

| Organ System | Main Organs | Function |
|--------------|-------------|----------|
| Digestive system | Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, intestines, liver, pancreas | Breaks down food, absorbs nutrients |
| Circulatory system | Heart, blood vessels, blood | Transports substances around body |
| Respiratory system | Lungs, trachea, bronchi, diaphragm | Gas exchange |
| Nervous system | Brain, spinal cord, nerves | Control and coordination |
| Excretory system | Kidneys, bladder, ureters | Removes waste products |
| Reproductive system | Ovaries/testes, uterus | Produces offspring |
| Skeletal system | Bones, cartilage | Support, protection, movement |
| Muscular system | Muscles | Movement |
| Endocrine system | Glands (pituitary, thyroid, etc.) | Hormone production and regulation |
| Immune system | White blood cells, lymph nodes, spleen | Defence against pathogens |

[DIAGRAM: Overview of major human organ systems]

### Level 5: Organism

**Definition:** A complete living thing made up of all organ systems working together.

- All organ systems are interdependent
- Failure of one system affects others
- Examples: humans, dogs, oak trees, bacteria (single-celled organism)

## Worked Example: The Digestive System

**Level: Organism** → Human

**Level: Organ System** → Digestive system

**Level: Organs** → Stomach, small intestine, large intestine, liver, pancreas

**Level: Tissues** (in the stomach):
- Muscle tissue (churns food)
- Epithelial tissue (lining, secretes mucus)
- Glandular tissue (produces enzymes and acid)
- Connective tissue (supports structure)

**Level: Cells** (in stomach lining):
- Epithelial cells
- Mucus-secreting cells
- Enzyme-secreting cells (chief cells)
- Acid-secreting cells (parietal cells)

## Worked Example: The Leaf

**Level: Organism** → Plant

**Level: Organ System** → Shoot system (stems, leaves, flowers)

**Level: Organ** → Leaf

**Level: Tissues:**
- Upper epidermis (protection)
- Palisade mesophyll (photosynthesis)
- Spongy mesophyll (gas exchange)
- Lower epidermis with stomata (gas exchange control)
- Xylem (water transport)
- Phloem (sugar transport)

**Level: Cells:**
- Palisade cells (contain chloroplasts)
- Guard cells (control stomata)
- Epidermal cells (protection)
- Xylem vessels (water transport)
- Phloem sieve tubes and companion cells (sugar transport)

[DIAGRAM: Hierarchical breakdown of a leaf showing all levels]

## Practical Applications

### Medicine
- Understanding organ systems helps diagnose diseases
- Organ transplants rely on understanding tissue compatibility
- Tissue engineering aims to grow replacement organs

### Agriculture
- Understanding plant organ systems improves crop yields
- Knowledge of root systems helps with irrigation
- Understanding leaf structure helps optimise photosynthesis

## Common Exam Questions

- Define the term 'tissue'
- Put these in order: organ, cell, organism, tissue, organ system
- Name two tissues found in the stomach/leaf
- Explain the relationship between cells, tissues, and organs

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** Blood is an organ
- **Reality:** Blood is a tissue (connective tissue). The circulatory system is an organ system

- **Misconception:** Skin is a tissue
- **Reality:** Skin is an organ - it's made of multiple tissues (epithelial, connective, muscle, nervous)

- **Misconception:** All organisms have organ systems
- **Reality:** Single-celled organisms (like bacteria and some protists) are just one cell - they don't have tissues, organs, or organ systems

- **Misconception:** Plants don't have organ systems
- **Reality:** Plants do have organ systems - the root system and shoot system

## Practice Questions

1. State the correct order of organisation from simplest to most complex. (1 mark)

2. Define the term 'organ'. (2 marks)

3. Name two tissues found in the human heart. (2 marks)

4. Name the organ system that includes the lungs and explain its function. (3 marks)

5. Using the stomach as an example, explain how cells, tissues, and organs are related. (4 marks)

6. Describe the levels of organisation in a plant leaf, from cells to organ. Include examples of cells and tissues at each level. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Cell | Basic structural and functional unit of life |
| Tissue | Group of similar cells performing a specific function |
| Organ | Structure made of different tissues working together |
| Organ system | Group of organs working together for a major function |
| Organism | A complete living thing |
| Epithelial tissue | Tissue that covers surfaces and lines cavities |
| Connective tissue | Tissue that supports, connects, or separates other tissues |
| Muscle tissue | Tissue that contracts to cause movement |
| Nervous tissue | Tissue that transmits electrical impulses |

## Summary

- Living organisms are organised in a hierarchy: cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organism
- A tissue is a group of similar cells working together
- An organ is made of different tissues working together
- An organ system is a group of organs performing a major function
- Both animals and plants show this hierarchical organisation
- Understanding levels of organisation is essential for understanding how organisms function
